sections.h2: How do you sell a house fast in Glendale Heights, Illinois?
sections.html:
To sell fast in Glendale Heights, start the village's transfer inspection application at least 21 days before closing, because that single step sets the earliest realistic closing date for any buyer, cash or financed. After that, the choice is between listing, selling privately, or accepting an as-is cash purchase.

  • A listing can reach the most buyers, but the house has to pass the village's inspection process like any other.
  • A private sale saves the commission and leaves the contract, disclosures and scheduling to you.
  • An as-is cash sale is common for houses with code problems, tenants or an estate, and the buyer can sign the village's guarantee of compliance for many checklist items.

Glendale Heights is a village in DuPage County and a far west suburb of Chicago. It is almost entirely residential, so most sales here are of single-family houses, townhouses, duplexes and condominiums, and the village's rules are written around those property types.

sections.h2: What is Glendale Heights like for home sellers?
sections.html:
Glendale Heights is a compact, diverse suburb of 32,655 people, according to the Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate, down from 33,176 at the 2020 census. It covers about 5.4 square miles of land, so houses sit close together and the village is easy to cross.

For 2020 to 2024 the Census Bureau reports a median owner-occupied home value of $261,700, an owner-occupied rate of 64.4 percent, 11,196 households and 2.93 people per household. Median gross rent was $1,590, median household income was $86,545, and workers averaged 26.7 minutes to get to work. Over half of residents age 5 and older, 58.1 percent, speak a language other than English at home, and 37.9 percent of residents are foreign-born.

The village grew out of farmland. Builders began putting up houses in 1958 on farms along Glen Ellyn Road north of North Avenue, and the village incorporated in 1959. It was first named Glendale because it sits between Glen Ellyn and Bloomingdale, and the word Heights was added in March 1960 for the roughly 100 foot rise created by the Valparaiso Moraine. Houses from the first building decades are now well past 50 years old, so roofs, furnaces and electrical panels deserve a look before you list.

sections.h2: Which employers and schools shape the Glendale Heights market?
sections.html:
Manufacturing and food production give the village a working base. The village's 2022 financial report listed Spraying Systems Co. as the largest employer at about 1,000 employees, followed by Cornelius at about 500 and Kronos Foods at about 400, with Super Target and Jewel-Osco among the retail employers.

Three K to 8 districts serve the village, and all feed into Glenbard Township High School District 87. Marquardt School District 15 covers the eastern part and feeds mainly into Glenbard East. Queen Bee District 16 sends students to Glenbard North and Glenbard West. Glen Ellyn School District 41 covers a portion of the village, and its students attend Abraham Lincoln School, then Hadley Junior High, and later Glenbard West.

The Glenside Public Library District serves the village, and Pace routes 711 and 715 connect it to Wheaton and other destinations. Because the district lines cut across the village, check the district for your street before you describe a school in a listing or offer letter.

sections.h2: What does Glendale Heights require before a house can transfer?
sections.html:
Glendale Heights requires a real estate transfer inspection for most sales, and the owner must file for a certificate of compliance at least 21 days before the proposed transfer, along with a plat of survey dated within one year. The inspection is visual only and does not replace a private home inspection.

Glendale Heights transfer inspection application fees as listed by the village
Property typeApplication fee
Single-family residential$100
Multi-family building, up to 6 units$200, plus $10 for each unit over 6
Commercial or industrial, up to 10,000 square feet$300

Here is the sequence the village lays out for sellers:

  • Community Development inspects the property and gives you a report of items to correct. You can fix them and request a re-inspection, or the purchaser can sign a Guarantee of Compliance for items authorized on the checklist.
  • Pay any money you owe the village, such as unpaid building or code invoices, lien filing fees, parking tickets and rental fees.
  • At the Finance Department, pay the final water bill, submit the stamp form, a copy of the deed and the state PTAX-203 declaration, then pay the transfer tax of $3 for every $1,000 of value or fraction thereof.

The sample checklist shows what inspectors look at: GFCI outlets in kitchens and baths, smoke and carbon monoxide detectors, window and door operation, panel and flue condition, a sump pump that discharges to the yard, and a fire-rated self-closing door between an attached garage and living space. A re-inspection can turn up items missed the first time, and the village may require an escrow to secure corrections. Call Community Development at 630-260-6030 and Finance at 630-260-6000 with questions.

sections.h2: Do Glendale Heights rental licensing rules affect a sale?
sections.html:
Yes. All residential rentals in the village must hold an annual license and be inspected each year, so a rental house or condo has an extra layer of paperwork at sale time. The transfer form asks whether the property was or will be used as a rental, and the checklist warns that a rental inspection is more stringent than the transfer inspection.

The village sets the license fee by property type: $200 for a single-family condominium, $300 for a single-family rental house, townhouse or duplex, and for apartment complexes $100 per building plus $50 per unit. Applications and fees are due by February 1 each year, and licenses expire January 31. A late renewal adds $25 per month, and a re-inspection fee of $75 can apply when an inspection is missed or cancelled late. Owners schedule inspections with their tenants by calling 630-260-6030.

If you own a rental here, clear any unpaid license or inspection fees before you apply for the transfer stamp, because the village will not issue it while rental fees remain owed.

sections.h2: How are DuPage County property taxes handled for Glendale Heights sellers?
sections.html:
DuPage County bills 2025 taxes in two installments, due June 1 and September 1, 2026, and the bills went out on April 29, 2026. A payment after a due date carries 1.5 percent per month in interest, and delinquent bills were mailed on October 21, 2026, after a pre-delinquent notice on September 28.

The county lists a homestead improvement exemption of up to $25,000 of assessment increase for four years, a senior homestead exemption, a disability exemption and veterans exemptions. The township assessor named on your tax bill answers valuation questions and handles the residential exemption, and the county Board of Review hears appeals filed within 30 days after your township's assessment roll is published. Evidence should include three or more comparable properties, and decisions usually arrive the following March.

Selling or refinancing sometimes leads to a double payment, because a title company or lender and the owner each pay the same bill. The county refunds a duplicate payment only to the person who made it, using a notarized affidavit and proof of payment, so tell your lender and title company which of you is paying.

faqs.q: How early should I start the Glendale Heights transfer inspection?
faqs.a: At least 21 days before the proposed closing. The village requires the application and a plat of survey dated within one year, and the application fee for a single-family home is $100.

faqs.q: Who pays the Glendale Heights transfer stamp?
faqs.a: The village's instructions are addressed to the seller, who completes the stamp steps at the Finance Department. The tax is $3 for every $1,000 of value or fraction thereof, and the deed, PTAX-203 and final water bill are part of the packet.

faqs.q: What happens if the inspection finds problems?
faqs.a: You receive a report of items to correct, and you may fix them and ask for a re-inspection. A purchaser may instead sign a Guarantee of Compliance for authorized checklist items, and the village may require an escrow.

faqs.q: Do I need a rental license to sell a rented house in Glendale Heights?
faqs.a: A rental house needs its annual license while it is rented, with renewals due February 1. Resolve unpaid rental fees first, since outstanding amounts owed to the village must be paid before the stamp.

faqs.q: Which office do I call about Glendale Heights taxes or exemptions?
faqs.a: Call the DuPage County Treasurer at 630-407-5900 for bills and payments, and the Supervisor of Assessments at 630-407-5858 for exemptions and appeals. Your township assessor, named on the bill, covers the residential exemption.
